prior_knowledge.concept: Keeping a pad-held route open while the other hero is affected by a bubble is recombined here as a two-barrier crossing followed by a later Isp launch.

evidence.claim: This room wires one Isp hold to both barriers, starts repeating bubbles from that pad, and requires a second bubble interaction after Pac clears the beam.

mechanics.fact: Only Isp activates HOLD, and it remains active only while Isp is on the pad; it opens both vertical barriers, which block Pac. Pac must pass both while Isp stays put.

evidence.claim: Isp-only HOLD is a hold-activated pad wired to both barriers; both barriers block Pac, so Isp must stay on the pad while Pac passes them.

mechanics.fact: While HOLD is active, the bubble launches repeatedly from the pad area. Pac can intercept a bubble from above for a top bounce and cross to the shelf above the far beam; the first interaction can leave Pac STICKY briefly but does not invalidate the route.

common_mistakes.mistake: Pac jumps into the first bubble before the team has stabilized the crossing, releasing Isp from HOLD.
common_mistakes.consequence: The barriers close and the early browser case shows Isp falling back to the HOLD pad; Pac is still on the starting side and needs the bubble cycle again.
common_mistakes.recovery: Isp lands back on HOLD, which reopens the barriers; the recorded correction completes with zero retries. The correction was one extra 16 ms right-input after a sampled endpoint fell short, so that exact micro-adjustment is build/tick-specific.

evidence.claim: The early-jump attempt records gate closure, Isp return to HOLD, zero retries, and the later ordinary-input correction.

evidence.locator: text:The early-jump source trace ended with Isp x859.25/y314 and Pac x896.75/y464, still playing.

common_mistakes.mistake: Isp receives FLOAT but misses the high landing.
common_mistakes.consequence: Isp returns to the safe floor/HOLD area instead of reaching the upper exit; Pac can wait at the low route.
common_mistakes.recovery: The next bubble is available; Isp can regain FLOAT and retry the upper landing without a retry/death in the recorded case.

evidence.claim: The missed-landing case records Isp back on the floor/HOLD, then a later FLOAT, upper landing, and completion with zero retries.

confidence_reason: Current source defines the causal mandatory route and recovery affordances. Focused ordinary-keyboard route and mistake cases establish feasibility and cheap retries but are from an older frozen browser build; they are not novice-human evidence or current-build acceptance. First-pass screenshots remain idle-only, and the exact ease of discovering the ordered handoff is unmeasured.

confirmed: The first pass correctly read an ordered catch/let-through relationship and a likely Isp-holder/Pac-crossing division from the idle cues.
The bubble effects and Isp HOLD pad were visible earlier at level_02; first pass correctly treated the basic bubbles as familiar.
The canvas contains no observed route, mistake, or feedback; no first-pass observation is retroactively promoted to a witnessed action.
missed_mechanics: HOLD opens both barriers at once and is the bubble launcher; Isp must remain there while Pac bounces through the two Pac-only barriers.
Pac’s first bubble interaction leaves STICKY, then Pac’s safe shelf position clears the beam so Isp can leave the pad and use a later bubble for FLOAT to the upper exit.
Missed landing and premature bubble cases can recover on the safe floor/HOLD with no retry in focused browser evidence.
incorrect_inferences: No decisive wrong mechanic claim was recorded; the first-pass suggestion that the holder might release or hand off the barrier was incomplete because the hold must remain active until Pac is beyond both barriers.
changed_judgments: Execution changed from unknown to 2 because ordinary keyboard evidence shows one Pac top-bounce/shelf landing and one Isp FLOAT/upper landing; a sampled endpoint needed a small correction, so moderate execution is more defensible than either no demand or sustained precision.
Timing changed from unknown to 1 because the source exposes a repeatable bubble cycle and the missed-interaction cases recover on later cycles; the waiting/sequence is not a narrow one-shot window.
Hazards changed from unknown to 0 because the source route has a continuous floor and no authored hazards, while both tested failures return safely to floor/HOLD.
Recovery changed from unknown to 1 because early gate closure and missed upper landing each have a demonstrated no-retry retry path.

Novelty increased from 1 to 2: the base hold and bubble effects are old, but the exact sequence—hold for Pac across two barriers, then release into a second bubble route for Isp—is a new transfer/recombination.
Clarity remains 2: the source supplies a direct route, but the idle cues only imply one-holder/order and do not expose the hold-to-bubble and clear-beam dependency.
unresolved: Whether novice pairs infer the necessary Pac-before-Isp ordering from the current dialogue and layout.
Whether the older-build trajectory/tick margin generalizes to the current frozen build, and whether shared-keyboard simultaneous inputs feel reliable to two humans.
The browser cases are focused scripted cases with a synthetic unlock fixture, not a measured novice run or full campaign journey.

single_operator_note: One operator would need to maintain Isp on HOLD while steering/jumping Pac with a separate key cluster, then shift back to Isp and coordinate the later FLOAT. The two keyboard clusters are distinct, but simultaneous two-hero execution may add attention and hand-switching burden; this is not included in the two-human ratings.
